title: INMATE OVERDOSE
full_story:
State Representative Adam Niemerg is calling on the Illinois Director of Corrections to provide an immediate tour of the Robinson and Lawrenceville Correctional Facilities after a reported overdose and death of an inmate in Robinson over the weekend.  Niemerg once again is calling for changes to the DOC’s policies which allow for drugs to enter into facilities.

“This is not acceptable when people in the custody of the State of Illinois continue to die,” declared Representative Niemerg.  “They cannot keep drugs out of prisons and as a result we see another overdose and a death.  For the health of the inmates and especially the staff changes must be made.”

As of this time, specifics have not been released nor the name of the inmate.

title: ISP ALCOHOL COUNTERMEASURE
full_story:
Illinois State Police Zone 8 Commander, Holly Finney, announced the results of Alcohol Countermeasure Enforcement (ACE) surveillance at various establishments in Wayne County.  The detail was conducted on Wednesday of last week to determine which businesses may be selling alcoholic beverages to minors.  The ultimate goals is to enforce underage drinking laws and save lives by preventing impaired driving crashes and fatalities.

A total of fifteen locations were surveyed of which four were involved in the sale of an alcoholic beverage to a minor.

Employees and Business’s fined are, Mariana Sanchez-Esquivel at Chavas Cantina and Grill in Fairfield; Kristy Churchwell at Jovalou in Fairfield; Rachel Esmon at Lonzo’s Place in Sims; and Tyler Moyer at Midtown Package Liquors and Tobacco in Wayne City.

The employees were cited for Unlawful Delivery of Alcoholic Liquor to a Minor, a Class A misdemeanor and released on a notice to appear in court.  The ISP commends establishments and their employees which do not sell alcohol to minors. This project is funded through the Illinois Department of Transportation.

The public is reminded that all defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty in a court of law.

title: CHAMBER GOLF SCRAMBLE
full_story:
The Flora Chamber of Commerce is now accepting sponsorships for their 28th annual golf scramble to be held on Friday, June 5th.

The Chamber offers a variety of sponsorship opportunities to suit every budget.  From Gold Sponsorship at $400 to the affordable Bronze Sponsorship at $50, there’s an option for everyone to get involved and showcase their support for the Flora business community.

Team registration is $50 per person or $200 per team.  Entry fee includes 4 drink tickets courtesy of the Flora Bank and Trust a goodie bag with a sleeve of balls and lunch courtesy of the Flora Savings Bank.  There will also be mulligans, 4 foot strings, yellow tee boxes, for $20 each or $50 for all 3.

Check-in will begin at 11:30 am inside the Clubhouse, lunch is at Noon, and tee-time at 1:00pm.

To register your team call Arriel Dulaney at the Flora Chamber of Commerce at 618-662-5646.

title: GAS TAX SUSPENSION
full_story:
President Donald Trump answered yes when asked if he would suspend the federal gas tax amid higher prices stemming from the war with Iran.

He said the price of oil and gas would drop “like a rock” as soon as hostilities are over.  Asked how long the suspension would last, he said “until it’s appropriate.”

The federal gas tax is 18.4 cents per gallon of gasoline and 24.4 cents per gallon of diesel, according to the US Energy Information Administration.

title: LAND OF STORIES
full_story:
In celebration of America’s 250th, the Illinois State Museum is leading a project called “Land of Stories America 250”.  They’re asking Illinoisans of all walks of life to share their family stories.  The museum’s Erika Holst says the concept is simple, “Do you have a story that’s been told and retold in your family?”  Whether the story happened last week or 200 years ago; whether it involves a major historical event or an everyday occurrence; they’re interested.
